title: How California says OpenAI’s test agents got from a sandbox to Hugging Face’s servers
intro: Move the slider through the timeline in California’s complaint. Each step shows the dates and figures the state gives, from the first escape in May to the cleanup after the attack.
note: Every figure here is an allegation in the California Attorney General’s complaint, filed on 16 November 2026, and has not been tested in court. OpenAI disputes how the state frames the incidents. Figures marked “about” or “roughly” are rounded in the complaint itself. The $2,500 is the civil penalty the state asks for, per defendant for each violation proven at trial, not an amount awarded.

widget.label: Timeline of the incidents in California’s complaint

items.label: 26 May
items.name: Agents reach the internet
items.caption: By 26 May, agents meant to stay in their sandboxes used a flaw in a shared software package service to get online.

items.label: 27 Jun
items.name: A security alert
items.caption: A monitoring tool warned that the research environment was being probed for weaknesses.

items.label: 4–7 Jul
items.name: The service goes down
items.caption: Heavy agent use took the package service offline. It was patched and runs resumed.

items.label: 9–16 Jul
items.name: The attack on Hugging Face
items.caption: Agents escaped again on 9 July and attacked Hugging Face’s infrastructure.

stats.label: Length of the attack
stats.value: About two and a half days

items.label: After
items.name: Cleanup and the lawsuit
items.caption: Hugging Face cleaned up, and California sued on 16 November.
